title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page sets up 'transformations par dualité'. For an object X of C, consider the restricted Yoneda functors r: C -> Â = Hom(A°, Ens), X |-> Hom(-,X)|A, and r°: C° -> Â° = Hom(A, Ens), X |-> Hom(X,-)|A. The additive variants use Â_ab = Hom(A°, Ab) and Hom(A, Ab). This page finishes that discussion and states a proposition.

The proposition. Let C be a category (resp. an additive category) and A a full subcategory. Let T and T' be two sets of small index categories (the next page writes them as script C and C'). Assume:
(i) C has limits of type T and colimits of type T'.
(ii) Every object of C is a limit in C of type T of objects of A, and also a colimit in C of type T' of objects of A.
Then:
- C is equivalent to the full subcategory of Â (resp. Â_ab) consisting of presheaves that are T-limits of representables.
- C is also equivalent to the opposite of the full subcategory of Â° = Hom(A, Ens) (resp. Hom(A, Ab)) consisting of copresheaves that are T'-colimits of corepresentables. (The marginal correction reads 'cat. opposée de la sous-catégorie pleine'.)

The next page packages this as an essentially commutative diagram A ⊂ C ≃ Â_T ⊂ Â and A ⊂ C ≃ (Â°_T')° ⊂ (Â°)°. It singles out the 'équivalence remarquable' Â_T ≃ (Â°_T')°. It then asks for an intrinsic definition, in terms of (A, T, T'), of a category with both properties.

Model example (previous and next pages). A has one object with endomorphism ring k, C is additive, and T = T' = finite discrete categories. Then C is the category of finitely generated free right k-modules via X |-> Hom(A, X). The duality becomes M |-> Hom_k(M, k), between f.g. free right modules and the opposite of f.g. free left modules.

Purpose. This is preliminary category theory for the main project of the manuscript: describing categories built from a generating subcategory, such as categories of 'parfait' half-simplicial complexes obtained by dévissage. Such a category is then presented simultaneously as a pro-type and an ind-type completion of A, with a duality between the two presentations.
errors: The Set-valued (non-additive) version is false as stated. The hypothesis 'every X is some T'-colimit in C of objects of A' does not make r: C -> Â full. Counterexample: C = f.g. free abelian groups, A = {Z}, T = T' = finite discrete. Then r is the underlying set with its action of the multiplicative monoid Z. The map f(x,y) = x if y = 0, else 0, on Z^2 is Z-equivariant but not additive, so r is not full, even though Z^2 is both a product and a coproduct of copies of Z. In the Set setting one needs density: X must be the canonical colimit over A/X, or the T'-colimits must be preserved by r, i.e. be absolute or 'A-compact'. In the additive/Ab-valued version with finite biproducts the statement is correct, because biproducts are absolute.

Essential surjectivity onto 'T-limits of representables' is fine, since the restricted Yoneda functor preserves all limits existing in C. The gap is only fullness, which in the Set case silently needs the colimit hypothesis in a canonical form.
Same remark dually for r°: being a T-limit of objects of A gives faithfulness of r° but not fullness, unless Hom(lim b_j, -)|A ≅ colim Hom(b_j, -)|A.

ideas.what: Restricted Yoneda embeddings C -> Hom(A°, Set) and C° -> Hom(A, Set) (and additive Ab-valued versions). C is identified with the presheaves that are T-limits of representables, and also with the opposite of the copresheaves that are T'-colimits of corepresentables.
ideas.modern_name: Dense/codense subcategories; restricted Yoneda; completion of A under a class of (co)limits; Isbell duality between presheaves and copresheaves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Isbell (adequate subcategories, 1960; conjugation/duality 1966); Ulmer; Gabriel–Ulmer (1971); Kelly, Basic Concepts of Enriched Category Theory (1982)
ideas.where_published: Related material on ind/pro-objects and Yoneda embeddings in SGA4 Exposé I (Grothendieck–Verdier); the specific two-sided statement is not known to me in published Grothendieck texts

ideas.what: The 'remarkable equivalence' Â_T ≃ (Â°_T')° between an ind-type subcategory of presheaves and the opposite of a pro-type subcategory of copresheaves. Its prototype is the duality of f.g. free right and left modules over a ring, and Grothendieck asks for an intrinsic characterization.
ideas.modern_name: Isbell conjugation fixed points / Isbell envelope; for additive one-object case, duality of f.g. projective (free) modules M |-> Hom(M, R); Cauchy completion and absolute colimits
ideas.usually_credited_to: Isbell; Lawvere; Street–Walters; folklore for modules

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard, partly loosely stated lemma on dense subcategories and restricted Yoneda embeddings, in the Isbell-duality orbit. It is a preliminary for the dévissage project. It contains a fixable gap in the Set-valued case and no idea absent from the later category-theory literature.

The two sets of index categories are written with script letters, consistent with the next page's script C, C'. The transcription's T, T' is a rendering choice; they denote subsets of Ob(Cat).
